deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page, headed 'Lagranges Lehrsatz'): x is defined implicitly by x = t + u·φ(x). Then ∂x/∂t = 1/(1−uφ'(x)) and ∂x/∂u = φ(x)/(1−uφ'(x)). Hence for any function f, ∂f(x)/∂u = φ(x)·∂f(x)/∂t (*). If F' = φ·f', i.e. F = ∫φ(x) df(x), then ∂f/∂u = ∂F/∂t.

This page. Goal: the u-derivatives of ψ(x) for an arbitrary ψ, i.e. the coefficients of ψ(x) as a power series in u (Lagrange's series).

Step 1. Take f = ψ in (*): ∂ψ(x)/∂u = ∂/∂t [∫ φ(x) ψ'(x) dx].

Step 2. Take f = F1 := ∫φ dψ. Then f' = φψ', and the associated F is ∫φ·φψ' dx = ∫φ^2 dψ. So ∂F1/∂u = ∂/∂t ∫φ^2 dψ. Differentiating Step 1 by u and interchanging ∂u and ∂t (implicit, mine) gives ∂²ψ/∂u² = ∂/∂t ∂F1/∂u = ∂²/∂t² ∫φ(x)^2 ψ'(x) dx. (Gauss writes φx^2 for (φx)^2.)

Step 3. Induction (Gauss only says 'u. allgemein'; the inductive step, applying (*) to F_k = ∫φ^k dψ with F_k' = φ^kψ', is mine): ∂^nψ/∂u^n = ∂^n/∂t^n ∫φ(x)^n ψ'(x) dx. Carrying out one t-derivative of the integral gives ∂^{n−1}/∂t^{n−1} [φ(x)^n ψ'(x) ∂x/∂t].

Step 4. The derivatives are wanted at u = 0, where x = t identically in t, so ∂x/∂t = 1. Since the remaining derivatives are in t only, u = 0 can be set first. This gives [∂^nψ(x)/∂u^n] at u=0 = d^{n−1}/dt^{n−1} [φ(t)^n ψ'(t)].

Implicit consequence (stated on the next page, not here): ψ(x) = ψ(t) + Σ_{n≥1} u^n/n! · d^{n−1}/dt^{n−1}[φ(t)^n ψ'(t)]. This is the Lagrange inversion series.
errors: The interchange of ∂/∂u and ∂/∂t, and the induction step, are used without comment. Both are legitimate for analytic functions.
The first equation uses d instead of ∂ (dψx/du). This is a purely notational inconsistency.

In the last expression of the general line, the image shows an extra '∂' before φx^n ('∂^{n−1}. ∂φx^n.ψ'x.∂x/∂t'). Read literally this would be one derivative too many. The intended and correct expression is ∂^{n−1}[φ(x)^n ψ'(x) ∂x/∂t]/∂t^{n−1}. It is probably a slip or residue of the ∂^n·∫ form.
The page gives only the derivatives. The factor 1/n! and the constant term ψ(t) of the Taylor series in u are left implicit (they appear on the next page).

results.what: For x = t + uφ(x): ∂^nψ(x)/∂u^n at u=0 equals d^{n−1}/dt^{n−1}[φ(t)^n ψ'(t)], derived via the PDE ∂f/∂u = φ(x)∂f/∂t and the representation ∂^nψ/∂u^n = ∂^n/∂t^n ∫φ^n dψ
results.modern_name: Lagrange inversion theorem / Lagrange–Bürmann formula (Laplace's proof via the identity ∂F/∂u = φ ∂F/∂t)
results.usually_credited_to: J.-L. Lagrange (1770); this method of proof is due to Laplace (1777) and was standard in textbooks such as Lacroix

deep.surprise_reason: A textbook reproduction (Gauss himself labels it 'Lagranges Lehrsatz') of the standard Laplace-style proof of Lagrange's series. These are student-era study notes with nothing non-standard.
